questions.q: According to this lesson's decision framework, what's the first question to ask when choosing an asynchronous tool?
options: Does this need to run on a recurring schedule, independent of any user action?
What color should the Lightning page button be?
Is Apex even allowed to run asynchronously in this org?
Does the org have more than 50 custom objects?
questions.explain: The first question is whether the work needs to run on a recurring schedule independent of a user action — if yes, Scheduled Apex belongs somewhere in the design.

questions.q: A requirement needs to process 2 million Lead records every night. What's the typical combination of tools for this?
options: A single future method handles the entire 2 million records directly
Scheduled Apex registers the nightly run, and its execute method calls Database.executeBatch on a Batch Apex class that does the actual processing in chunks
Queueable Apex alone, chained 2 million times
This cannot be done with any combination of asynchronous Apex tools
questions.explain: This is the most common real-world pattern: Scheduled Apex decides when the job runs, and its execute method kicks off a Batch Apex job, which is built specifically to process large volumes of records in per-chunk transactions.

questions.q: A multi-step process needs step two to only start after step one has fully committed, and step three only after step two commits. Which tool fits this requirement?
options: Chained Queueable jobs, where each job's execute method enqueues the next step as its last action
A single future method covering all three steps in sequence
Scheduled Apex running all three steps once a year
This requirement cannot be satisfied by any asynchronous Apex tool
questions.explain: Chained Queueable jobs are built exactly for this: each job commits fully before enqueuing the next step, guaranteeing the ordering the requirement describes.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe the four asynchronous tools as 'composable' rather than mutually exclusive?
options: Because real designs frequently combine them — e.g., Scheduled Apex triggering Batch Apex, or an early Queueable step handling a callout before a later step continues the work
Because only one of the four tools can ever be used in a single org at a time
Because Salesforce requires every org to use all four tools together on every job
Composability only applies to Batch Apex, never to the other three tools
questions.explain: The tools are building blocks that commonly combine — Scheduled Apex deciding when a Batch Apex job runs, or a Queueable chain handling a sequence of dependent steps — rather than being four separate, competing answers to the same question.

questions.q: A single Case needs a one-off callout fired to an external system when it closes, with only the Case Id needed as input. Which tools does this lesson say are reasonable fits?
options: Only Batch Apex, since any callout requires per-chunk transactions
A future method with callout=true, or Queueable Apex implementing Database.AllowsCallouts if a trackable job Id is also wanted
Only Scheduled Apex, since callouts can never happen outside a scheduled context
This scenario has no valid asynchronous solution and must run synchronously
questions.explain: For a small, simple, one-off callout with only primitive inputs, a future method with callout=true is a reasonable fit, and Queueable Apex with Database.AllowsCallouts is an equally valid, more modern alternative if job tracking is also wanted.
